nodes.summary: There are infinitely many sequences $(s_n)_{n \ge 0}$ of positive integers with all of the following properties: each value is taken by $s_n$ for only finitely many $n$; there are integers $c_0, c_1, c_2$ with $c_0 \ne 0$ and $s_{n+3} = c_0 s_n + c_1 s_{n+1} + c_2 s_{n+2}$ for all $n \ge 0$; there are no integers $d_0, d_1$ with $s_{n+2} = d_0 s_n + d_1 s_{n+1}$ for all $n \ge 0$; and $s_k$ is not a sum of two…
nodes.title: Third-order recurrences with infinitely many terms not sums of two prime powers

nodes.summary: The integer $2$ is a sum of two prime powers, since $2 = 2^0 + 2^0$.
nodes.title: $2$ is a sum of two prime powers

nodes.summary: An integer $n$ is a sum of two prime powers if $n = p^a + q^b$ for some primes $p$ and $q$ and some natural numbers $a$ and $b$. Since the exponents may be $0$, the number $1 = p^0$ counts as a prime power here.
nodes.title: Sums of two prime powers

nodes.summary: Let $(L_n)_{n \ge 0}$ be the Leonardo numbers, the generalized Leonardo numbers $L_{1,n}$ with parameter $1$, given by $L_0 = L_1 = 1$ and $L_{n+2} = L_{n+1} + L_n + 1$. There are infinitely many natural numbers $k$ such that $L_k$ is not a sum of two prime powers.
nodes.title: Infinitely many Leonardo numbers are not sums of two prime powers

nodes.summary: If $n$ is an integer with $n < 2$, then $n$ is not a sum of two prime powers, since every prime power $p^a$ is at least $1$.
nodes.title: Integers below $2$ are not sums of two prime powers

nodes.summary: Let $(E_n)_{n \ge 0}$ be the Perrin sequence, given by $E_0 = 3$, $E_1 = 0$, $E_2 = 2$ and $E_{n+3} = E_{n+1} + E_n$. There are infinitely many natural numbers $k$ such that $E_k$ is not a sum of two prime powers.
nodes.title: Infinitely many Perrin numbers are not sums of two prime powers

nodes.summary: Let $(a_n)_{n \ge 0}$ be the shifted Padovan sequence, given by $a_0 = 1$, $a_1 = 0$, $a_2 = 1$ and $a_{n+3} = a_{n+1} + a_n$, so that $a_{n+2} = P_n$ is the $n$-th Padovan number, where $P_0 = P_1 = P_2 = 1$ and $P_{n+3} = P_{n+1} + P_n$. There are infinitely many natural numbers $k$ such that $a_k$ is not a sum of two prime powers.
nodes.title: Infinitely many Padovan numbers are not sums of two prime powers

nodes.summary: Let $(T_n)_{n \ge 0}$ be the Tribonacci sequence, given by $T_0 = 0$, $T_1 = 0$, $T_2 = 1$ and $T_{n+3} = T_{n+2} + T_{n+1} + T_n$. There are infinitely many natural numbers $k$ such that $T_k$ is not a sum of two prime powers.
nodes.title: Infinitely many Tribonacci numbers are not sums of two prime powers
